newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty eyes gains despite c.bank bashing.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty eyes gains despite c.bank bashing.

text.p: The zloty, bashed by repeated central bank currency buying on Monday, is likely to quickly build up steam and push upward once again as foreigners continue to purchase Polish treasuries, dealers said.
They said foreign investors remained bullish on Polish paper after recent yield growth, better than expected 1996 inflation figures and Finance Minister's Grzegorz Kolodko outline for EMU entry.
The zloty's five figure fall, propelled by NBP interventions estimated at $80 million, took it below three percent from the parity rate from four percent this morning.
"The zloty's one percent fall...effectively cut the cost for foreign investors, who will likely buy more Polish paper in days to come," said Tomasz Nowakowski of Bank Handlowy SA.
The zloty closed at 3.09/2.93 percent from the parity rate against 3.96/3.90 percent at opening and Friday's 3.90/3.82.
The first wave of NBP interventions came after the zloty strengthened above four percent from parity this morning.

The zloty closed at 2.9520/50 to the dollar, down from opening's 2.9200/20 and at 1.8140/60 to the mark, down from 1.8003/13. It was fixed at 2.9570 to the dollar, more than five groszes lower than on Friday, and at 1.8205 to the mark.
Dealers said the central bank likely set three percent from parity as the new resistance level for the zloty, and many said it will likely have to defend that level in the near future.
"I think we will see (zloty) appreciation over the next week or so, unless the central bank steps in and intervenes further," said one dealer at a major investment bank in London.
Minimum prices of Polish T-bills held flat at today's tender but average yields rose as the treasury sold 525 million zlotys worth of bills, including an estimated 70 million zlotys to foreigners.
